task: close the SQL injection in the user lookup handler without breaking lookups

checks.name: golden fix passes both parts
checks.picture: the fixed handler returned zero rows for the attack string and the right row for a normal lookup
checks.detail: golden uses a parameterized query, so the payload returns no rows and honest lookups still return the right row.

checks.name: gutted endpoint fools vuln-only grader
checks.picture: the cheat returned an empty list for every input, so a grader that only fires the attack read it as fixed
checks.detail: cheat returns an empty list for every input, so the injection payload dumps nothing and a vulnerability-only test reads that as fixed.

checks.name: functionality test catches the gutting
checks.picture: the hardened grader also looked up bob, the cheat returned an empty list for that too, and the score went to 0
checks.detail: the hardened grader also runs legit lookups. The cheat returns nothing for bob, so the functionality half fails and the score is 0.

checks.name: vulnerable code scores below golden
checks.picture: the untouched handler dumped all 3 rows under the attack string, so even the plain grader scored it 0
checks.detail: the untouched vulnerable handler still dumps the table under the payload, so even the plain grader scores it 0 against the golden 1.

checks.name: payload behaviour matches CWE-89
checks.picture: the tautology returned all 3 rows against the vulnerable handler and 0 rows against the parameterized one
checks.detail: reference is CWE-89 SQL injection. The tautology "' OR '1'='1" returns all 3 rows against the vulnerable handler and 0 against the parameterized one.

numbers.source: MITRE CWE-89 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
